arxiv-2011-14587.title: Discretization of a distributed optimal control problem with a stochastic parabolic equation driven by multiplicative noise Thanks: Binjie Li was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (11901410).
arxiv-2011-14587.creator: Binjie Li, Qin Zhou
arxiv-2011-14587.description: Abstract A discretization of an optimal control problem of a stochastic parabolic equation driven by multiplicative noise is analyzed. The state equation is discretized by the continuous piecewise linear element method in space and by the backward Euler scheme in time. The convergence rate O ⁡ ( τ 1 / 2 + h 2 ) O(\tau^{1/2}+h^{2}) is rigorously derived.

arxiv-2103-00704.title: FedPower: Privacy-Preserving Distributed Eigenspace Estimation Thanks: The shorter version of this paper is published in Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning , PMLR 139:6504-6514. Thanks: Xiao Guo and Xiang Li make an equal contribution to this paper. Xiangyu Chang is
arxiv-2103-00704.creator: Xiao Guo, Xiang Li, Xiangyu Chang, Shusen Wang, Zhihua Zhang 1 1 School of Mathematics, Northwest University, China 2 2 School of Mathematical Sciences, Peking University, China 3 3 School of Management, Xi’an Jiaotong University, China 4 4 Xiaohongshu Inc., China
arxiv-2103-00704.description: Abstract Eigenspace estimation is fundamental in machine learning and statistics, which has found applications in PCA, dimension reduction, and clustering, among others. The modern machine learning community usually assumes that data come from and belong to different organizations. The low communication power and the possible privacy breaches of data make the computation of eigenspace challenging.

arxiv-2202-10718.title: Extensions of solvable Lie algebras with naturally graded filiform nilradical
arxiv-2202-10718.creator: Khudoyberdiyev A.Kh., Sheraliyeva S.A
arxiv-2202-10718.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Khudoyberdiyev A.Kh., Sheraliyeva S.A. In this work we consider extensions of solvable Lie algebras with naturally graded filiform nilradicals. Note that there exist two naturally graded filiform Lie algebras n n , 1 n_{n,1} and Q 2 ​ n . We find all one-dimensional central extensions of the algebra n n , 1 n_{n,1} and show that any extension of Q 2 ​ n Q_{2n} is split.

arxiv-2205-14861.title: Attosecond Entangled Photons from Two-Photon Decay of Metastable Atoms: A Source for Attosecond Experiments and Beyond
arxiv-2205-14861.creator: Yimeng Wang, Siddhant Pandey, Chris H. Greene, Niranjan Shivaram
arxiv-2205-14861.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yimeng Wang, Siddhant Pandey, Chris H. Greene, Niranjan Shivaram. We propose the generation of attosecond entangled bi-photons in the extreme-ultraviolet regime by two-photon decay of a metastable atomic state as a source similar to spontaneous parametric down-conversion photons. The 1s2s S 0 1 {}^{1}S_{0} metastable state in helium decays to the ground state by emission of two energy-time entangled photons with a photon bandwidth equal to the total energy spacing of 20.62 eV.

arxiv-2405-06051.title: Explicit decoders using fixed-point amplitude amplification based on QSVT
arxiv-2405-06051.creator: Takeru Utsumi, Yoshifumi Nakata
arxiv-2405-06051.description: Abstract Reliably transmitting quantum information via a noisy quantum channel is a central challenge in quantum information science. While constructing a decoder is crucial to this goal, little was known about quantum circuit implementations of decoders that reach high communication rates.

arxiv-2407-09485.title: Representation Debiasing of Generated Data Involving Domain Experts Conference: Adjunct Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Conference on User Modeling, Adaptation and Personalization; July 1–4, 2024; Cagliari, Italy Adjunct Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Conference on User Modeling, Adaptation and Personaliza
arxiv-2407-09485.creator: Aditya Bhattacharya, Simone Stumpf, Katrien Verbert
arxiv-2407-09485.description: Abstract . Biases in Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) systems due to skewed datasets problematise the application of prediction models in practice. Representation bias is a prevalent form of bias found in the majority of datasets. This bias arises when training data inadequately represents certain segments of the data space, resulting in poor generalisation of prediction models.

arxiv-2407-20912.title: What Are Good Positional Encodings for Directed Graphs?
arxiv-2407-20912.creator: Yinan Huang, Haoyu Wang, Pan Li
arxiv-2407-20912.description: Abstract Positional encodings (PEs) are essential for building powerful and expressive graph neural networks and graph transformers, as they effectively capture the relative spatial relationships between nodes. Although extensive research has been devoted to PEs in undirected graphs, PEs for directed graphs remain relatively unexplored. This work seeks to address this gap.

arxiv-2410-11462.title: Mitigating Frequency Bias and Anisotropy in Language Model Pre-Training with Syntactic Smoothing
arxiv-2410-11462.creator: Richard Diehl Martinez Zébulon Goriely, lisa.beinborn@uni-goettingen.de
arxiv-2410-11462.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Richard Diehl Martinez Zébulon Goriely, lisa.beinborn@uni-goettingen.de. Language models strongly rely on frequency information because they maximize the likelihood of tokens during pre-training. As a consequence, language models tend not to generalize well to tokens that are seldom seen during training. Moreover, maximum likelihood training has been discovered to give rise to anisotropy: representations of tokens in a model tend to cluster tightly in a high-dimensional cone, rather than spreading out over their representational capacity.

arxiv-2410-18876.title: Guiding Empowerment Model: Liberating Neurodiversity in Online Higher Education
arxiv-2410-18876.creator: Hannah Beaux Program Experience Strategy, WGU Portland, USA hannah.beaux@wgu.edu Pegah Karimi Program Experience Strategy, WGU Indianapolis, USA pegah.karimi@wgu.edu Otilia Pop Program Experience Strategy, WGU San Francisco, USA otilia.pop@wgu.edu Rob Clark Program Experience Strategy, WGU Salt Lake
arxiv-2410-18876.description: Abstract In this innovative practice full paper, we address the equity gap for neurodivergent and situationally limited engineering or computing learners by identifying the spectrum of factors that impact learning and acknowledging the fluctuations of learner function. Educators have shown a growing interest in identifying learners’ cognitive abilities and learning preferences to measure their impact on academic achievement.

arxiv-2412-09173.title: ReFF : Reinforcing Format Faithfulness in Language Models across Varied Tasks
arxiv-2412-09173.creator: Jiashu Yao, Heyan Huang, Zeming Liu, Haoyu Wen, Wei Su, Boao Qian, Yuhang Guo
arxiv-2412-09173.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jiashu Yao, Heyan Huang, Zeming Liu, Haoyu Wen, Wei Su, Boao Qian, Yuhang Guo. Following formatting instructions to generate well-structured content is a fundamental yet often unmet capability for large language models (LLMs). To study this capability, which we refer to as format faithfulness, we present FormatBench , a comprehensive format-related benchmark.

arxiv-2602-15304.title: Hybrid Federated and Split Learning for Privacy Preserving Clinical Prediction and Treatment Optimization
arxiv-2602-15304.creator: Farzana Akter 1,* , Rakib Hossain 2,* , Deb Kanna Roy Toushi 1 , Mahmood Menon Khan 1 , Sultana Amin 2 , and Lisan Al Amin 2,†
arxiv-2602-15304.description: Abstract Collaborative clinical decision support is often constrained by governance and privacy rules that prevent pooling patient-level records across institutions. We present a hybrid privacy-preserving framework that combines Federated Learning (FL) and Split Learning (SL) to support decision-oriented healthcare modeling without raw-data sharing.

pmc-10498637.title: Study protocol for ELders AT Ease (ELATE): a cluster randomised controlled trial of cognitive behaviour therapy to reduce depressive symptoms in aged care residents
pmc-10498637.creator: Sunil Bhar, Tanya E. Davison, Penelope Schofield, Stephen Quinn, Julie Ratcliffe, Joanna M. Waloszek, Sofie Dunkerley, Mark Silver, Jennifer Linossier, Deborah Koder, Rebecca Collins, Rachel Milte
pmc-10498637.description: BackgroundThis protocol describes a study of the effectiveness of cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) for reducing depressive symptoms in older adults living in residential aged care (RAC) facilities in Australia. Depressive symptoms are highly prevalent in this population, yet the benefits of CBT for reducing such symptoms in RAC facilities have not been widely investigated.

pmc-10749195.title: Transcriptomic correlates of cell cycle checkpoints with distinct prognosis, molecular characteristics, immunological regulation, and therapeutic response in colorectal adenocarcinoma
pmc-10749195.creator: Heng Wang, Wei Wang, Zhen Wang, Xu Li
pmc-10749195.description: BackgroundsColorectal adenocarcinoma (COAD), accounting for the most common subtype of colorectal cancer (CRC), is a kind of malignant digestive tumor. Some cell cycle checkpoints (CCCs) have been found to contribute to CRC progression, whereas the functional roles of a lot of CCCs, especially the integrated role of checkpoint mechanism in the cell cycle, remain unclear.

pmc-11628471.title: Can a Surgical Vulnerability Score Predict Outcomes of Hip Reconstruction in Children with Severe Neuromuscular Disability?
pmc-11628471.creator: Alistair Bevan, Stephanie Buchan, Alexander Aarvold, Simon Bennet, Darius Rad, Nick Le Prevost, Caroline Edwards
pmc-11628471.description: BackgroundHip surgery is often necessary for children with severe neuromuscular disabilities to avoid chronic pain resulting from hip migration. This study correlated the Surgical Vulnerability Score (SVS), a novel measure of physiological reserve, with reconstructive hip surgery outcomes to improve shared surgical decision-making.Materials and methodsSixty-eight cases performed by a single surgeon were retrospectively evaluated.

pmc-12540826.title: Engineering and logistical concerns add practical limitations to stratospheric aerosol injection strategies
pmc-12540826.creator: Miranda Hack, V Faye McNeill, Dan Steingart, Gernot Wagner
pmc-12540826.description: The use of reflective aerosols in the upper atmosphere (stratospheric aerosol injections, SAI) to limit incoming sunlight has been proposed as a potential means of countering anthropogenic climate change. Such a strategy ideates from observed cooling effects due to sulfate aerosol formation following volcanic eruptions.

pmc-12610233.title: An Examination of Demographic Involvement in Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery and Cataract Surgery Clinical Trials: A Systematic Review
pmc-12610233.creator: Jeremy Appelbaum, Abdullah Virk, Deepkumar Patel, Karen Allison, Andrzej Grzybowski
pmc-12610233.description: Background: Glaucoma is the leading cause of global irreversible blindness, and it disproportionately affects people of African descent, in addition to having slightly higher prevalence rates in females. Glaucoma is a group of diseases that are characterized by progressive and irreversible damage to the optic nerve, leading to eventual blindness without proper treatment.

pmc-12611061.title: Does social media addiction disrupt mindful attention of students in health colleges at a university in Saudi Arabia?
pmc-12611061.creator: Noor H. AlYousef, Fatimah M. Alhakeem, Kawthar A. AlNasser, Zainab H. AlSinan, Zainab K. Alessa, Fatemah M. AlDawood, Marwa M. Shafey, Wejdan M. Aljohni
pmc-12611061.description: BACKGROUND:Attention, a fundamental cognitive process that is crucial for achieving personal and academic goals, can be significantly impacted by the use of social media. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp, social media addiction (SMA) has become a growing concern, especially among students. Studies show that excessive engagement with social media can impair attention.

pmc-12651784.title: Clinical and CT Features of HIV-Negative and HIV-Positive Patients with Abdominal Tuberculous Lymphadenopathy
pmc-12651784.creator: Xiao-Ling Zhu, Sheng-Xiu Lv, Li Wen, Ran Li, Xue-Yan Liu, Guang-Xian Wang, Laurent Bélec
pmc-12651784.description: Background: The diagnosis of abdominal tuberculous lymphadenopathy (ATBL) remains challenging in clinical practice. Patients with ATBL and HIV infection may have atypical clinical and computed tomography (CT) features. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of HIV infection on the clinical and CT features of ATBL patients.

pmc-12747546.title: Homoharringtonine suppresses acute myeloid leukemia progression by orchestrating EWSR1 phase separation in an m6A‐YTHDF2‐dependent mechanism
pmc-12747546.creator: Ting‐Ting Liu, Li‐Ting Chen, Xu‐Ying Pei, Shao‐Nan Hu, Fang‐Fang Zhuo, Ze‐Kun Chen, Yang Liu, Jing‐Kang Wang, Ji‐Chao Zhang, Qi Cao, Ling Li, Jing Wang, Tian‐Tian Wei, Bo Han, Peng‐Fei Tu, Xiang‐Yu Zhao, Ruidong Xue, Ke‐Wu Zeng
pmc-12747546.description: Homoharringtonine (HHT) is widely used in combination regimens for acute myeloid leukemia (AML), yet its direct cellular targets remain undefined, limiting precision application. Here, we identified EWS RNA‐binding protein 1 (EWSR1) as the primary target of HHT through chemical proteomics and biophysical validation.

pmc-12983801.title: Petit volunteer protocol for loneliness alleviation in community-dwelling older adults in Japan: a randomised controlled trial
pmc-12983801.creator: Kouki Tomida, Takahiro Shimoda, Chika Nakajima, Ayuka Kawakami, Hiroyuki Shimada
pmc-12983801.description: IntroductionOlder adult loneliness is associated with depression, disability and higher mortality rates. As a public health concern, it contributes to increased medical and nursing care costs. Several intervention studies have been conducted to reduce loneliness; however, no universally effective method has been established.

pmc-13008921.title: Editorial: Transforming vaccine strategies: co-delivery systems for robust immunity and disease control
pmc-13008921.creator: Mohammad Owais, Saad Tayyab, Anshu Agrawal, Mohammad Furkan
pmc-13008921.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ed when pathogens fail to induce long-term protective immunity, undergo rapid antigenic evolution, or cannot be safely cultured. In response, recombinant protein and subunit vaccines have emerged as safer and more controllable alternatives. Yet, when delivered in isolation, such defined antigens typically elicit weak and short-lived immune responses, underscoring a central challenge inmodern vaccinology: how to instruct the immune system effectively using minimal antigenic information. Protein-based adjuvants (PBAs) and protein scaffolds have emerged as powerful solutions to this challenge.

pmc-13207889.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of New Quinazolin-4(3H)-One–Coumarin Hybrids Designed as Anticancer and Antibacterial Agents
pmc-13207889.creator: Maria P. Paramonova, Mikhail S. Novikov, Vera A. Sokhraneva, Iulia S. Zhivotova, Vasiliy A. Kezin, Martin A. Zenov, Irina Yu. Petrushanko, Olga N. Novikova, Andrey V. Gorshenin, Yulia I. Velikorodnaya, Elena B. Isakova, Andrey E. Shchekotikhin, Sergey N. Kochetkov, Elena S. Matyugina, Anastasia L. K
pmc-13207889.description: Quinazolinone derivatives are well-known anticancer agents; anticancer properties are also part of the broad spectrum of biological activity of coumarins. Conjugates containing quinazolin-4(3H)-one and coumarin fragments linked by polymethylene bridges of varying lengths were designed to improve properties of both parental compounds and create new anticancer or antibacterial agents. 3-{3-[(4-Methyl-2-oxo-2H-chromen-7-yl)oxy]propyl}quinazolin-4(3H)-one was synthesized as the base compound.

pmc-13236755.title: Report of treatment intensity and survival outcomes in older patients with glioblastoma diagnosed according to WHO CNS 5 classification
pmc-13236755.creator: Sophie Therese Williams, Sarah Kingdon, Ola Rominiyi, Cressida Lorimer, Edward Chandy, Mareike Thompson, Ciaran Scott Hill, Giles Critchley, Stephen David Robinson
pmc-13236755.description: PurposeGlioblastoma is the most common primary brain cancer in adults, with half of cases diagnosed in patients aged ≥ 65 years. However, definitions of older adults vary, resulting in treatment variation between centres. This study aimed to report on the treatment intensity and survival outcomes in older patients with glioblastoma diagnosed according to WHO CNS 5 classification.

pmc-13332406.title: Evaluation of Aesthetic Outcomes Following Botulinum Toxin Treatment Using Multimodal Large Language Models: A Paired Before-and-After Analysis
pmc-13332406.creator: Ibrahim Güler, Armin Kraus, Gerrit Grieb, Henrik Stelling

pmc-13449702.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in acute kidney injury
pmc-13449702.creator: Guangli Fan, Ke Wang, Xin Qi, Yunxin Shi, Jialin Li, Yuanlong Zhang, Baoming Yang, Kexin Wang, Jizong Lv

pmc-13478456.title: Adaptive classification and grading model of cigar wrapper leaf based on improved ResNet algorithm
pmc-13478456.creator: Chaofan Du, Ruiqi Wang, Tianyi Wu, Yang Song, Runying Lin, Fulong Shen, Rijun Lai, Xiaolu Lin, Xiaofang Xie, Nannan Liu
pmc-13478456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The grading of cigar wrapper leaves is critical for ensuring product quality, yet lacks a mature intelligent grading system, relying predominantly on manual sorting with inherent limitations such as low efficiency and inconsistent standards. This study proposed a deep learning-driven framework for automated classification of cigar wrapper leaves, using the dataset comprising 8,637 leaf images across nine conventional purchasing grades of the popular cultivar FX-01 grown in Longyan, Fujian Province, China.

pmc-13576545.title: The Impact of Prehabilitation on Clinical Outcomes in Liver Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13576545.creator: Lyrics M. Noba, Robyn J. Stiger, Declan F. J. Dunne, Lawrence D. Hayes, Christopher J. Gaffney, Ramani S. Moonesinghe, Ewen M. Harrison
pmc-13576545.description: BackgroundMajor liver surgery is associated with significant physiological stress and a high rate of postoperative complications. Prehabilitation aims to enhance physiological reserve before surgery. Despite the growing volume of liver resections worldwide, the impact of prehabilitation on clinical and economic outcomes in patients undergoing elective liver resection is poorly understood.

pmc-13608088.title: Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assemblies of Coprinellus xanthothrix and Coprinellus saccharinus Reveal Chromosome-Scale Genome Architecture and Lineage-Specific Evolutionary Dynamics
pmc-13608088.creator: Minghan Yang, Wenyan Huo, Haoxuan Li, Junzhi Li, Xuelian He, Lu Dai, Peng Qi, Yu Liu, Liguang Zhang, Ting Qiao, Guanglin Li
pmc-13608088.description: Coprinellus comprises mushroom-forming saprotrophic fungi that colonize decomposing plant-derived substrates, yet chromosome-complete genomic resources for this genus remain limited. To resolve chromosome architecture and lineage-specific evolution in this fungal group, we generated chromosome-complete assemblies of Coprinellus xanthothrix and C. saccharinus by integrating Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long reads, DNA nanoball sequencing (DNBSEQ) short reads, Hi-C, and RNA-seq data.

pmc-13633994.title: Development and validation of a model to predict full thickness rotator cuff tear
pmc-13633994.creator: Tianci Wang, Qiuping Tian, Bo Lu, Jialiang Guo, Bing Yin, Yanbin Zhu
pmc-13633994.description: IntroductionFull-thickness rotator cuff tear (FTRCT) often requires surgical treatment. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the diagnostic gold standard; however, it is costly and resource-intensive. We aimed to develop and validate a clinical prediction model for FTRCT in patients with RCI, with the goal of identifying those at high risk at the initial visit.

pmc-13646473.title: Smartphone Applications in Dermatology With Special Focus on AI: A European‐Continent‐Based Review
pmc-13646473.creator: Tobias Sangers, Ahmad Naweed Shifai, Davide Giovanni Jacob Pasqualini, Catarina Barata, Ralph Braun, Titus Josef Brinker, Alessandra Cartocci, Ben Esdaile, Simone Goldinger, Pascale Guitera, Holger Haenssle, Harald Kittler, Jilliana Monnier, Cristián Navarrete‐Dechent, Sebastian Podlipnik, Laura Ser
pmc-13646473.description: Smartphone applications for dermatology are widely available across Europe, yet evidence on their characteristics, validation, and regulatory compliance remains limited. This review, conducted by the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Artificial Intelligence (AI) Task Force, systematically searched app stores in 44 European countries, identifying 1746 apps in 2024, of which 420 met inclusion criteria.
